output.brief: The rise in mishandled bags is mainly not a handler problem. Since 1 September, Corvane's check-in tags printed on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 11.8% of the time, against about 1.5% before. Pelion bags, which Tessaly also handles, and Corvane transfer tags stayed normal. On 14–16 Oct, counters that used old Brackwater stock from stores read at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick stock stayed at 12%. The extra bags go to the manual encode desk, where waits roughly quadrupled, and 91% of the missed bags reached the lateral after it closed. Auto-read bags show no rise. Don't send the breach notice or withhold fees. It would punish the wrong party, and the evidence contradicts it. Switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater now. About five weeks of stock is held and the contract is valid to 31 Dec. Then watch the no-read and mishandling rates. Test whether Fennick stock is defective or just needs different printer heat settings, and use the Teyra bulletin for that. Hold any claim against Fennick until that test is done. An extra encode workstation is a reasonable stopgap. I'm fairly confident in the main finding. The open question is whether the stock or the printer settings are at fault.
